Reproject, mask and composite GLASS rasters for a region

Source: R/read_process.R
glass_process.Rd

Takes granule paths (or an already-read SpatRaster stack), applies glass_read() cleanup, groups granules by composite date, merges tiles per date, reprojects the result to the CRS of roi, crops and masks, and optionally collapses layers with a function (e.g. a temporal mean). This is the parameterised version of the legacy glass_process.R script.

Usage

glass_process(
  input,
  roi,
  target_crs = NULL,
  res = NULL,
  method = "cubic",
  fun = "none",
  outfile = NULL,
  product = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

input

Granule paths of one variant, or a SpatRaster stack (then fill/scale handling is assumed done).

roi

Region of interest (sf/sfc); its CRS is the target CRS.

target_crs

Optionally override the target CRS.

res

Output resolution in target-CRS units (default: automatic).

method

terra::project() resampling method, e.g. "cubic" (default) or "near" for categorical data.

fun

"none" (default) keeps one layer per granule date; "mean", "max", "min" or a function collapse layers.

outfile

Optional GeoTIFF path to write.

product

Registry variant key for glass_read().

...

Passed on to glass_read().

Value

A processed SpatRaster.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
files <- glass_fetch("LAI_MODIS_250M", "2018-08-01", "2018-12-31",
                     tiles = "h28v05", out_dir = "data/glass/lai")
mean_lai <- glass_process(files, roi = shanghai_sf, outfile = "lai_mean.tif")
} # }
